title: As asked (A): the block module, below-the-block reader rule and brief composer
description:
Piece A of LIN-4345's approved plan (revision 2). It **lands first**, and nothing blocks it. Every change is inert until some ticket carries an `## As asked` block, so A is safe to land on its own. Once piece B (LIN-4345's write side) starts sealing tickets, the readers are already correct.

## What landed (plan steps 1, 2 and 7)

Implemented and merged in [https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2345](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2345>) (squash `fdd57fe9`, deployed 7 Nov 2026):

* `lib/as-asked.js`: seal, split, check, `readFact`, `askedText`, `hasMarkerLine`. It is the only place the two markers are spelled out.
* Below the block wins: every census reader goes through `readFact`. `condensePlan` never condenses inside the block.
* The brief composer: `composeBrief` and `briefQuoteEnd` in `lib/brief.js`, wired into `generateBrief`, both mocks and both brief parsers. First-line readers use the block's words.

The plan slice was implemented as approved. Six reasoned departures are recorded in the PR body and on LIN-4345 (comment `9c36e8e1`). In close-out, the brief system prompt was changed to name the heading through `AS_ASKED_HEADING` (review finding 1).

The full pre-prune description, including this piece's plan slice, is preserved in the task snapshots (snapshot `9a7e3ffa`) and in the comment trail.

## Testing: witnesses 1 and 2 (each must fail before the change)

* **Witness 1: the words reach a step unchanged.**
  * Feed `generateBrief` a stub model that paraphrases the ask. The served brief must start with `## As asked` followed by the block's exact bytes, on the proxy route and the session route, fresh and cached.
  * One case has an ask containing `## Current`. `briefCurrentSection` must return the model's section, not the person's.
  * On Linear the quoted block keeps its backslash escapes, and the promise is byte for byte against what is stored. If a Linear-escaped case compares through `normalizeEscaping`, the test says why.
* **Witness 2: below the block wins.**
  * A sealed child with `plan-review due: no` in its block and `plan-review due: yes` below reads `yes` in `assembleTrailFacts` and in round-trips. With nothing below the block, it reads `no`.
  * Session fit and the plan section follow the same rule.
  * `condensePlan` leaves a plan heading inside the block untouched.
  * An unsealed ticket reads as today.

## Acceptance

* `lib/as-asked.js` exists and is the only place the markers are spelled out.
* Every reader in the census uses the fact reader.
* The brief composer is wired into `generateBrief`, both mocks, and both brief parsers.
* Witnesses 1 and 2 pass and are shown failing before the change.
* `npm test` is green, and the prompt-size budget (`tests/unit/prompt-size-budget.test.js`) is not exceeded.

---

**Session fit:** fits one session

**Plan-review due:** no — covered by LIN-4345's approving plan-review (comment 23006cda-4b9f-4268-9392-a82d804ea7dd, rev 2)

**Grounding commit:** `e63c2f69` (main, 7 Nov 2026; the plan and all three plan-review verdicts were checked against it; main had not moved when this breakdown ran at 10:40 UTC)

**Starting point:** your starting point is the approved plan on the parent, LIN-4345 ("Every step reads what the person asked"). Read it in full under `## Implementation Plan` (revision 2) in LIN-4345's description, and read the approving verdict (comment 23006cda, 10:36 UTC on LIN-4345), including its "Notes for the builder". Follow the plan. Where the code shows the plan is wrong, change course and say so in a comment on LIN-4345. The person's own words and the "Done looks like" are at the top of LIN-4345's description. Repository: JKershaw/LinearViewer (Harbour).

comments.body:
## Implementation summary: LIN-4351

**PR:** https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2345 (branch `feat/lin-4351-as-asked-block`, targets main). Not merged; review and close-out own that.

**Head:** `c7cd33f3ad475ee073cd73e116c23de8352385b3`

**CI:** all green on that head (Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4, Secret scan, CI success): https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/actions/runs/42368146332
- The first run, on `fa6f2ae2`, was red in Unit tests. The hermetic:proxy arm's `HTTPS_PROXY` bypassed witness 1's `fetch` stub.
- Fixed in `c7cd33f3` by clearing the proxy variables in each test, as `feedback-title.test.js` does. No assertion changed.

**Tests:**
- **Full `npm test` (local, macOS, `fa6f2ae2`):**
  - Unit stage: 24017 pass / 0 fail.
  - Playwright: 2002 passed, 1 skipped, 2 failed. Neither failure is from this change: `lin-4010-home-opened-task.spec.js:230` passed when re-run on its own (flaky), and `live-console.spec.js:444` (a pixel width, 334 vs 319) fails the same way on main `e63c2f69` on this machine. All four E2E shards pass in CI.
- **CI unit arms, local, at `c7cd33f3`:** `test:hermetic:keyed` and `test:hermetic:proxy` each passed 24017/24017 and opened zero non-loopback sockets.
- **Prompt-size budget:** 16/16, with no ceiling changed. `lib/prompt-contract.js` is 3643 bytes, under its 3656 ceiling.

**What landed (plan steps 1, 2, 7):**
- **Step 1:** `lib/as-asked.js`, the only place the two markers are spelled out: seal, split, check, `readFact`, `askedText`, `hasMarkerLine`.
- **Step 2:** every census reader goes through `readFact`, so the text below the block wins:
  - `recommendation-facts` (`extractSessionFit`, `assembleNodeFacts`, `assembleTrailFacts`, and `condensePlan`, which never condenses inside the block)
  - `file-pointer`'s `extractPlanSection`/`extractPlanPaths`
  - round-trips' gateDue
  - follow-on-ratio's `hasPlanMarker`
  - the module comments on both measures, and the rule in the `prompt-contract.js` reader table
- **Step 7:** `lib/brief.js` gains `composeBrief` and `briefQuoteEnd`.
  - They are wired into `generateBrief` and both mock builders, so the proxy route, the session route and the task page serve the quoted brief.
  - The parsers read after the quote, and the system prompt is updated. The brief model stays `openai/gpt-5.4-mini`.
  - First-line readers show the person's first line.

**Witnesses:** each was shown failing before the change. Witness 2 had 8 failures before, plus the plan-comment case; it now passes 22/22. Witness 1 had 10 failures before and now passes 16/16. The module tests pass 32/32. The evidence is in the PR body.

**Departures from the plan:** recorded on LIN-4345 (comment `9c36e8e1`) and in the PR body.

**Status:** LIN-4351 stays In Progress for review.

## Review — LIN-4351

Reviewed PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2345 at head `c7cd33f3ad475ee073cd73e116c23de8352385b3`. The branch has 4 commits on `e63c2f69`, and `origin/main` is still at `e63c2f69`, so the ticket's grounding commit has not gone stale.

CI: green on `c7cd33f3`: Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4, Secret scan and CI success ([run 42368146332](https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/actions/runs/42368146332)). Locally at the same head, the three new test files plus `prompt-size-budget.test.js` pass 86/86.

### Scope against the plan
The changes stay inside plan steps 1, 2 and 7. Every place the description names was changed, and nothing outside those places:
- `lib/as-asked.js`
- the census readers in `recommendation-facts` (:287, :333, :481/assembleTrailFacts, condensePlan), `file-pointer`, `follow-on-ratio` and `plan-review-round-trips`
- the reader-table rule in `prompt-contract.js`
- `composeBrief`, wired into `generateBrief` and both mock builders
- both brief parsers
- the three first-line readers

There is no write-side or stage-prompt work, which belongs to B and C. The six departures are recorded in the PR body and on LIN-4345 (comment `9c36e8e1`). Each one is reasoned, and none widens scope. The brief model stays `openai/gpt-5.4-mini`, and a test asserts it. No prompt-size ceiling changed (`prompt-contract.js` is 3643 bytes against a 3656 ceiling).

### Regression check
`git log` over the 10 changed source files shows no recent fix or revert to the same behaviour (recent commits are the cost read, LIN-4143 and LIN-4263). Since the ticket was created, main has had no commits to these paths.

### Is it one of a class?
I grepped `lib/` and `routes/` for every reader of the three code-read lines (`Implementation Plan`, the session-fit phrases, `plan-review due:`) and for first-line readers of `description`. Every code reader goes through `readFact` or `askedText`. The other hits are prompt prose (stage templates, completion signals), which piece C owns. There are no `generateBrief` callers beyond the ones that were wired; `scripts/eval/lin-263-spike4.mjs` calls it too and gets the composition for free. **No unhandled siblings.**

### Mutation checks
For each mutation I ran the three new test files, then reverted the mutation. The working tree is clean afterwards.

| Mutation | Failures |
|---|---|
| `readFact` ignores the block | 12 |
| `readFact` drops `{after}` | 3 |
| `generateBrief` without `composeBrief` | 9 tests, including proxy fresh/cached, proxy POST, session POST/GET |
| `briefCurrentSection` without `briefQuoteEnd` | 1 |
| `briefWithoutCurrent` with quoteEnd forced to 0 | 1 |
| `condensePlan` condenses inside the block | 1 |
| gateDue reads the whole description | 1 |
| `extractPlanSection` reads the whole description | 1 |
| `extractSessionFit` reads the whole description | 2 |
| trail planReviewDue reads the whole text | 4 |
| trail sessionFit reads the whole text | 1 |
| proxy mock without `composeBrief` | 1 |
| session mock without `composeBrief` | 1 |
| `toStackHeadline` without `askedText` | 1 |
| proxy mock summary without `askedText` | 1 |
| `hasPlanMarker` back to the whole description | **0** (stays green) |

The surviving `hasPlanMarker` mutation is expected and is not a finding. It is a presence test, so with the default pattern its answer cannot change. The PR says so, the module comment says so, and its test is a pin, not a witness. Every load-bearing witness goes red when its own code path is removed.

### Findings
1. **The marker is spelled out a second time in runtime text.** `lib/brief.js:45`: `BRIEF_SYSTEM_PROMPT` contains the literal `` \`## As asked\` ``. The acceptance criterion says `lib/as-asked.js` is the only place the markers are spelled out. Comments that mention the heading are fine, but this string ships to the model, and it would go stale if the marker ever changed. **Fix for close-out:** in `lib/brief.js`, add `AS_ASKED_HEADING` to the existing `./as-asked.js` import. In `BRIEF_SYSTEM_PROMPT` (already a template literal), replace `` \`## As asked\` `` with `` \`${AS_ASKED_HEADING}\` ``. The output bytes do not change. Then run the as-asked-brief tests: the system-prompt assertion should stay green.

The rest of the checklist passes: security (pure functions, no new I/O), error handling (null and empty inputs are handled), code style, and performance (one extra linear scan per read).

### What CI Did Not Prove
- **The task page renders a composed brief correctly.** Inside: step 7, "every cache reader gets the composed brief … the task page". Unit tests cover `briefCurrentSection` and `briefWithoutCurrent`, but no test drives `render-task-page.js:630` with a composed brief. **Before the merge:** close-out renders the task page once with `model.brief.body = composeBrief(sealAsAsked('…## Current\nperson text'), mockFourSections)` and `model.summary = briefCurrentSection(thatBody)`. Right: the header shows the model's `## Current`, and the brief panel shows the quoted block followed by Constraints, Open questions and Changelog. Wrong: the header shows the person's text, or the panel loses the quote or repeats Current.
- **The real brief model still produces four parseable sections under the new system prompt.** Inside: step 7 and departure 5. The prompt change applies to every brief, sealed or not, and CI only runs stubbed models. **After the deploy:** force-regenerate the brief of one unsealed ticket (POST `/api/proxy/brief/LIN-4345`). Confirm the four headings are present, `briefCurrentSection` is non-null, and Current does not reframe the ask. Whether the model leaves a *sealed* block un-restated can only be observed once piece B seals a ticket. That check goes with B's first live seal: GET that ticket's brief and confirm the block's words appear once, as the quote. **Rollback:** revert the squash commit of #2345. It is reversible because no data is persisted in a new shape, and briefs are re-hashed on the description.
- **Block detection matches how Linear actually stores a sealed body.** Inside: step 1's marker comparison after `normalizeEscaping`; every reader depends on it. The tests use synthetic escapes. Partial evidence: LIN-4345's stored description keeps `## ` headings and single-`*` italic lines unescaped, which is the end line's shape. Nothing can write a sealed body until piece B, so this is **after the deploy, at B's first live seal:** GET that issue through the proxy and assert `splitAsAsked(description)` is non-null and its `words` equal the filed body, compared after `normalizeEscaping`. Wrong: null, which means the readers silently fall back to reading the whole description.

### Verdict
Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger

The work is complete against steps 1, 2 and 7, and every witness was mutation-checked. Close-out should make the one-line fix in finding 1, run the task-page render check before the merge, and record the two post-deploy checks.

## Close-out — LIN-4351

**What merged:** https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2345, squash commit `fdd57fe9`, pinned with `--match-head-commit` to head `59ee7dc36f50dc9432c1b209d152c794a369dd4b`.

**Final CI:** green on `59ee7dc3`. Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4, Secret scan (source) and CI success all passed ([run 42369238679](https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/actions/runs/42369238679)). Main had not moved off `e63c2f69` before the merge.

**Deploy:** the harbour.cat footer shows `fdd57fe9`.

**Staleness check:** `origin/main` stayed at the grounding commit `e63c2f69` until this merge, so no referenced path changed after the ticket was created.

### Changes made after the approval
- **`59ee7dc3`** answers review finding 1 ("The marker is spelled out a second time in runtime text", `lib/brief.js:45`).
  - `AS_ASKED_HEADING` is added to the `./as-asked.js` import, and `BRIEF_SYSTEM_PROMPT` interpolates it in place of the literal `## As asked`.
  - The output bytes are unchanged: I captured the system prompt through `buildBriefMessages` before and after, and both hash to sha256 `46cc8966…`.
  - The as-asked module, readers, brief, `brief.test.js` and prompt-size-budget tests pass 95/95.

### Ledger
1. **The task page renders a composed brief.** Inside, before the merge. **Done.**
   - I rendered the real `renderTaskPage` over a `buildTaskPageModel` model (the golden test's running case). Its brief was `composeBrief(sealAsAsked('Make the brief quote me.\n\n## Current\nperson text…'), fourSections)`, and `summary` came from the loader's `briefCurrentSection`.
   - **Header:** shows the model's `## Current`, not the person's.
   - **Brief panel, in order:** `## As asked`, the person's words (including their own `## Current`), the end line, then Constraints, Open questions and Changelog. The model's Current is not repeated, and exactly one `## Current` remains: the person's.
   - **Mutation:** with `briefCurrentSection` changed to ignore `briefQuoteEnd`, the check fails because the header shows the person's text. The mutation was then reverted.
2. **The real brief model produces four parseable sections under the new prompt.** Inside, after the deploy. **Done for an unsealed ticket.**
   - At 11:55 UTC on `fdd57fe9` I force-regenerated with POST `/api/proxy/brief/LIN-4345`. The model was `openai/gpt-5.4-mini`.
   - The headings are exactly Current, Constraints, Open questions and Changelog. `briefQuoteEnd` is 0, as it should be for an unsealed ticket. `briefCurrentSection` from the landed code is non-null (802 chars).
   - Current does not reframe the ask: it states the remaining B/C work, and the open "whose words count" ruling sits under Open questions.
   - **Not run:** the sealed half, "the model leaves a sealed block un-restated".
     - What: GET a sealed ticket's brief and confirm the block's words appear once, as the quote.
     - Why: no ticket can carry a block until piece B (LIN-4352) seals one.
     - Who: LIN-4352's implementer or close-out, or the operator, at B's first live seal. This is recorded on LIN-4352 (comment `5c5ede0c`) and in the PR.
3. **Block detection matches how Linear stores a sealed body.** Inside, after the deploy. **Not run.**
   - What: GET the first sealed issue through the proxy and assert that `splitAsAsked(description)` is non-null and that its `words` equal the filed body after `normalizeEscaping`.
   - Why: nothing can write a sealed body until piece B.
   - Who: the same owners at the same moment, recorded in the same two places.
- **Rollback, named by review:** revert squash commit `fdd57fe9`. No data is persisted in a new shape, and briefs re-hash on the description.

**For the operator:** ledger items 2 (the sealed half) and 3 were not run. Both run at piece B's first live seal.

### Related tickets
- **LIN-4352 (B):** its blocker has landed. I commented the two checks that wait for its first live seal; it stays Todo.
- **LIN-4353 (C):** unchanged.
- **LIN-4345 (parent):** stays In Progress while B and C remain.

**Outside follow-ups:** none. Review's ledger had no outside items, so nothing was filed and no ruling was raised.

**Description:** I archived it first (`/brief?noRefresh=1`). I then verified that snapshot `9a7e3ffa` (captured 11:56:28 UTC) is byte-identical to the pre-prune description.
- **Pruned:** the "This piece's slice of the plan" section, replaced with a "What landed" stub that links the PR.
- **Kept:** the problem statement, the witnesses, the acceptance criteria, the session-fit phrase, the `Plan-review due:` line, the grounding commit and the starting point.

## Autopilot run summary — LIN-4351 (stepper, session 00c34f88)

**Arc:** implementation (4 warm beats in one session) → review → close-out. Every stage ran on `anthropic/claude-opus-4.8`, as the human asked.

**Beats (ROOT `f841149d`):**
1. **Ground, branch, `lib/as-asked.js`:** 30 tests, failing before the module existed and passing after; 3 deliberate breaks were each caught.
   - Challenge sent with beat 2: `readFact` treated `false` as absent. Fixed so that only null/undefined count as absent, with a test for block yes / below no reading no.
2. **Below-the-block reader rule across the census, plus witness 2:** 8 tests failed before the change; 22/22 pass after.
   - Challenge sent with beat 3: the beat had raised the `prompt-contract.js` byte ceiling. That raise was reverted; the file is now 3643 bytes against the unchanged 3656 ceiling.
3. **Brief composer, wiring, first-line readers, plus witness 1:** 10 tests failed before the change; 16/16 pass after.
4. **Full suite, PR, CI:** PR #2345 opened; unit suite 24017/24017; CI green on `c7cd33f3`.

**Review (`ccaafce5`):** Approve, conditional. 15 of 16 deliberate code breaks were caught by the tests; the one that stayed green is expected. One fix was named (`lib/brief.js:45`), plus 3 items CI could not prove.

**Close-out (`67ee7ed7`):** I checked each of these myself.
- **Fix:** made in `59ee7dc3`; the system prompt's bytes are unchanged.
- **Merge:** PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2345 merged at 11:47 UTC as `fdd57fe9`.
- **CI:** green on head `59ee7dc3` (run 42369238679) and on the merge commit `fdd57fe9` (Tests run 42369684928).
- **LIN-4351:** Done.

**What holds:**
- The block module, the reader rule and the brief composer are on main.
- Task-page rendering with a quoted brief was checked before the merge.
- A real gpt-5.4-mini brief still parses into its four sections after the deploy.

**What's left:** two checks could not run, because no ticket carries a block until piece B (LIN-4352) seals one.
- A sealed ticket's brief quotes the block once and the model does not restate it.
- `splitAsAsked` detects a sealed body as Linear stores it.

Both are recorded on LIN-4352 (comment `5c5ede0c`) for B's first live seal.

## Survey 1a (round 3)

**1. Why was this difficult?** It was not difficult in concept; the friction was in keeping old behaviour exact. "Below the block wins" sounds like one rule, but the readers each meant "found" differently:
- a presence boolean (`hasPlanMarker`);
- first match wins (`planReviewDue`);
- the last heading wins (`extractPlanSection`);
- a "yes" anywhere, matched by a loose regex (`GATE_DUE_MARKER` also matches "due: yesterday" and across a newline).

One `readFact` had to fit all of them without moving an unsealed ticket's answer. The rest was setup: the size ceiling covers source comments; the brief routes have no stub-model seam, so I stubbed `fetch` and registered a fake provider; and CI's proxy arm bypassed that stub.

**2. What I'd have done first.** I'd have listed what each reader returns when its line is absent, before writing `readFact`; that would have caught my `false`-means-absent bug. And I'd have read the CI workflow before writing a network stub.

**3. What I'd tidy.**
- **Two identical mock brief builders**, both now calling the composer. One should go.
- **Two regexes for one line:** `PLAN_REVIEW_DUE` and `GATE_DUE_MARKER` differ in looseness; merging them needs a note on the measure's comparability.
- **Route test harnesses** are copied across files.

**4. What the ticket would have been.** With code-read lines parsed in one place (a `descriptionFacts()` every reader used), the reader half would be one function and one test.

**5. What the ticket or plan got wrong.**
- **"Today the first match wins"** is true of only some readers; the plan section takes the last heading.
- **The round-trips witness** "block no, below yes → yes" could not fail before the change, because the regex already matched a yes anywhere. Only the inverse case was new behaviour.
- **"Lacks"** was never defined.
- **Plan comments** weren't considered: a plan heading inside the block would have hidden a plan posted as a comment.
- **"The composer exports where the block ends"** didn't say how a parser holding only the brief finds it. I reused the sealed shape.

**6. What it left behind.**
- **New:** `lib/as-asked.js`, a clean home.
- **In two places:** the rule, in `as-asked.js` with a pointer in `prompt-contract.js`.
- **Odd:** the brief now contains "Steps write below this line".
- **One caller:** `readFact`'s `{ after }` serves only `assembleTrailFacts`.
- **Unmeasured:** the brief prompt change reaches every ticket; nothing measures its effect.
- **Simpler:** `condensePlan` and the plan section stop at the block's edge.

**7. Did the larger scope pay?** For piece A, yes. The read/write/prompts split made the readers right before any block exists, and that ordering is the real safety. The cost was the brief half: witness 1's harness was most of the effort, and the prompt change belongs with piece C. I'd have drawn A as the module plus readers, with the brief composer as its own piece beside C.
